subject: Urgent: SOC2/SIG evidence request + incident notification
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finsecure.io>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: security@finsecure.io
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed anomaly + request for IR plan and SOC2/SIG evidence

Hi Neha,

Quick heads up from our platform security team: we observed a short-lived anomalous set of API calls originating from a small subset of IPs associated with a Redwood subdomain between 2026-04-06 22:34 UTC and 2026-04-06 22:41 UTC. At the moment we have no clear sign of data exfiltration, but our SOC team is initiating a formal review.

Could you please: 
- Confirm whether Redwood observed any related backend events for our tenant (FinSecure Inc.) during that window.
- Share your incident response plan (IR playbook) for suspected compromise involving hosted API keys.
- Provide your most recent SOC 2 attestation and completed SIG/CAIQ artifacts relevant to incident handling and logging.

We've attached our observed events log (FinSecure_observed_events.log) for your reference. Additionally, we may need a short post-incident summary once investigations are complete (timeline, root cause, mitigations). Can you also indicate an expected ETA for the initial confirmation and a follow-up postmortem?

Appreciate a rapid reply — we are coordinating with our procuring/ops teams and may need to pause some automated integrations until we get confirmation.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Security | FinSecure Inc.
email: alex.turner@finsecure.io
phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

Alex — thanks for flagging and for the log. We're treating this as high priority. 

High-level next steps from our side: 
1) I'll triage and confirm whether the event maps to any Redwood-hosted API keys for FinSecure and return an initial status within 2 hours.
2) Mina (security) will lead the technical investigation and will share relevant telemetry and timeline.
3) Rishi (legal) will advise on any disclosure or contractual steps; Marissa will coordinate communications with your CSM/account team.

Mina — can you pick this up and confirm whether there are backend traces (auth logs, token usage, or unusual KV cache activity) that align with the timestamps Alex provided? If you post an initial statement here I will forward to FinSecure and include the SOC2/SIG artifacts.

Alex — we will attach our IR playbook and most recent SOC2 attestation if available. If our initial check shows no tenant exposure we will still provide a short incident note and proposed mitigations.

Neha Kapoor

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finsecure.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed anomaly + request for IR plan and SOC2/SIG evidence

Neha / Alex — investigation update: 

Summary so far:
- We observed repeated 401/403 auth failures from the same IP cluster during 2026-04-06 22:33–22:42 UTC.
- No successful token exchanges or downstream data access tied to FinSecure tenant IDs in that window.
- No abnormal KV-cache evictions or model-weight telemetry associated with the tenant.

Actions performed:
- Correlated API gateway logs and auth provider logs; no sign of valid token use.
- Rotated any ephemeral service keys previously in scope for other tenants as precautionary measure.
- Increased logging retention for the FinSecure tenant for 30 days pending your review.

Deliverables attached to this message: 
- Redwood_IR_Playbook_v3.1.pdf (redacted public version of IR plan highlighting containment, notification, and postmortem cadence)
- SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf (PDF attestation; sensitive evidence packages will be provided via our audited share)
- SIG_Responses_2026-04-07.xlsx (answers to common SIG control areas; redactions applied where needed)

Drive link for full investigator-only artifacts (access granted to FinSecure security contact for 72 hours): https://drive.google.com/redwood/IR_Playbook_v3.1

Next steps we propose: 
1) We will provide an initial confirmation email now (no tenant access observed).
2) Follow-up technical packet (auth traces by request, timestamps, any revoked keys) available within 24 hours via secure share.
3) Formal post-incident write-up (timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, monitoring changes) aimed at 5 business days unless further analysis extends that window.

If you want immediate live collaboration we can stand up a short call with our on-call infra and your SOC — let me know a preferred time.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Thanks — that's helpful and appreciated. Quick notes: 
- We confirm receipt of the playbook, attestation, and SIG responses.
- For now our ops team will keep integrations paused until we review the secure artifacts (we've accepted the Drive link and downloaded the investigator packet).
- We would like the 24-hour technical packet (auth traces and any revoked-key list) and will schedule a 45-minute call to review tomorrow at 10:00 PDT if that works for your on-call.

Please send the secure share link for the technical packet when ready and flag any items that require a formal nondisclosure or additional legal agreement. We'll look out for the 5-business-day post-incident summary.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Alex
